headline: LLMs mine literature for chemical-effect and hepatotoxicity evidence
label: Llm Assisted Biological Literature Curation
summary: Automated LLM pipelines now convert full-text toxicology and biomedical literature into structured, queryable evidence for AOP and hepatotoxicity work.
synthesis: The common thread is LLM-based extraction from biological literature feeding structured, domain-specific resources. AOP-Smart-Finder pairs LLMs and retrieval-augmented generation in a human-AI hybrid framework to map biological events, key event relationships and AOP evidence across large corpora. AOPTK packages LLM-assisted retrieval and extraction of chemical-effect relationships from toxicological literature as open-source Python software. The automated hepatotoxicity pipeline mines PubMed and PMC full texts into a knowledge base of 189,212 findings across 17,002 chemicals. The dated gene-evidence tables are a different kind of resource: they support leakage-aware retrospective evaluation of gene prioritization and do not themselves describe LLM processing. What is new is the pairing of domain-specific curation with computational assistance at scale, applied to toxicology and adverse outcome pathway knowledge.
